REPORT: AI SEARCHES WHAT IT REMEMBERS
articles.summary: AI search visibility depends heavily on whether a model already remembers a brand before it searches the web. A new report found that remembered brands were searched 3.2 times more often than brands outside the model's memory, with search rates of 55.7% versus 17.4% across nearly 4,000 AI responses. Category authority built through press coverage, analyst mentions, partnerships, and consistent brand association appears to increase the odds that AI models will search for and recommend a brand. Strong live content still helps newer brands appear in AI searches, but building long-term brand recognition gives a more reliable path to visibility across future AI answers.

articles.title: WHEN MARKETING RUNS ITSELF
articles.summary: Self-improving marketing is already live, with AI systems running continuous loops that execute and refine their own work. In one case, an SEO loop ran every 2 hours for 9 weeks, while another saw organic sessions jump 85% alongside more efficient paid performance. Each cycle builds on the last, compounding gains over time. As execution becomes automated, the role of marketing shifts toward setting direction and judging outcomes, while the system handles ongoing optimization.

articles.title: BRIBES WORK: THE BEST WAY TO GROW YOUR EMAIL LIST THAT'S STILL UNDERUTILIZED
articles.summary: Growing an email list starts with creating discovery content on a consistent schedule and using lead magnets to capture subscribers. Instead of lengthy ebooks or courses, businesses should create quick, actionable resources like templates, swipe files, and checklists that solve a specific problem. These can be repurposed from existing newsletters, social posts, videos, or client materials. Testing new lead magnets monthly and promoting them through social channels, websites, and email flows helps find what drives conversions.

articles.title: CASE STUDY: HOW A WEBSITE REDESIGN DELIVERED THE BEST YEAR EVER FOR CHURNET VALLEY RAILWAY
articles.summary: A research-led website redesign can grow conversions without risking revenue when every change is validated through testing before launch. Churnet Valley Railway used user research to find specific friction points, then rolled out A/B tested updates one page at a time. The homepage redesign increased conversions by 5%, and reusing proven design patterns helped lift Breakfast Train bookings by 10%, Midweek Lunch Train bookings by 48%, and dining page conversions by 13%. The program also showed that practical information, customer FAQs, and richer visuals such as video can increase bookings, which helped the railway sell out its Christmas event after a 7% booking increase.

articles.title: HOW TINDER IS GETTING PEOPLE OFF THE APP AND INTO THE WILD
articles.summary: Tinder is trying to get its users out of the swipe screen and into cooking classes and mahjong nights instead. The feature grew out of research into Gen Z's post-pandemic social atrophy, letting users see who's attending an event beforehand and swipe on them afterward rather than in the moment to reduce the pressure of in-person rejection. Nearly 70% of eligible users engaged during a 60-plus event LA pilot, and it's now expanding to 26 cities across the US and Europe by September, one of Tinder's largest financial and engineering bets in a decade.

articles.title: JOSH GRANT WEBINAR: THE 30-DAY AI SEARCH PIPELINE RECOVERY SPRINT
articles.summary: Most brands optimize for Google while AI answers quietly reroute buyers elsewhere. On August 5, Josh Grant, founder of StackedGTM and former VP of Growth at Webflow, joins AirOps to break down the playbooks turning AEO into revenue this quarter, comparison pages, pricing pages, and third-party proof.

articles.title: ALERTMOUSE
articles.summary: Alertmouse is a lightweight brand monitoring tool that finds and tracks mentions across the web, including sources Google Alerts often misses. Users set up alerts in minutes, then receive filtered, prioritized results via email or API. It's built for marketers, founders, and creators who want signal without noise or enterprise bloat. Pricing is freemium, and your first alert is free forever. Paid plans are available for additional alerts and usage.

articles.title: WINNERS AND LOSERS OF AI SEARCH WITH KEVIN INDIG (WEBINAR)
articles.summary: AI search is changing what gets surfaced and cited, making traditional SEO metrics like rankings and traffic less reliable indicators of performance. Growth Advisor Kevin Indig will join AirOps Head of Search Marketing Josh Spilker on August 13 to explain how to measure visibility through citations and share of voice. They'll also cover why methods like last click attribution and prompt tracking can mislead.

articles.title: WHY HUMAN STORYTELLING OUTPERFORMS CHATBOTS (20 MINUTE PODCAST)
articles.summary: Katie Passarello, Co-Founder of PitchWell, explains how AI is changing public relations by making storytelling and media outreach more accessible. The discussion explores how businesses can improve visibility while maintaining the human experiences that make stories compelling. It also highlights why third-party credibility remains important as brands compete with the growing volume of AI-generated content.

articles.title: THE NO MARKETING PLG STRATEGY BEHIND CURSOR'S $60B ACQUISITION
articles.summary: Developers distrust campaigns but trust each other, so Cursor built its growth strategy around peer proof rather than paid promotion. It removed setup friction to create an immediate "wow" moment, shipped rough features in public instead of waiting for polish, and used a free tier to drive word of mouth while paid tiers converted engineers at companies like Shopify and OpenAI who started expensing it themselves. Cursor also turned community into its marketing department, paying 300 city-based ambassadors to run hackathons that double as tutorials, content, and recruiting all at once.
